summary: I hand-wrote `.taad/fitness.yaml` on slice/SL-022 from the five [Fact]s in `tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/ArchitectureRulesTests.cs`. It holds eight `must_not_match` entries, one per ([Fact], scope glob) pair. Every entry has single-quoted patterns with a leading `(?m)`, `including_comments: true`, a glob rooted at src/ or tests/, and the test's exemptions. A header names the test file as its twin and states the authoring rules. The design keeps tests out of the project, so each shape was checked in a scratch copy under %TEMP% by calling the committed engine's own `taad3.fitness` module and running xUnit against the same planted tree. On the worktree, Fitness reports '8 rule(s) checked against 33 file(s) read. Every declared rule holds.' with no rule that matched no files, and git does not ignore the file. All 17 planted violations failed the same rule in Fitness and in xUnit. The file names matched every time and the line numbers matched in 16 of 17. Nothing under src/ or tests/ changed, and the project's full suite still passes 86/86.

files.why: The rules file Fitness reads, with 8 must_not_match entries covering the 5 ArchitectureRulesTests rules. It has to be committed on the slice branch for validate to read it (spike 2). The builder does not commit, so the engine's commit_all carries it.

obligations.how: Each of the 20 yaml patterns is the xUnit string with `(?m)` added at the front and nothing else changed. None of them contains a `'`, so there was no quote escaping to do. The test compiles with RegexOptions.Multiline only, so `(?m)` is the only inline flag. No pattern has a `$` anchor, so nothing needed `\r?`. On parity, 17 violations were planted one at a time in a built scratch copy. Each was checked with the engine's fitness.check and with `dotnet test --no-build --filter ArchitectureRulesTests`, which reads the source text at run time. Both failed or passed on the same rule and file every time. Line numbers matched in 16 of 17. The exception was a `using System.Windows;` at Scanner.cs:7, after a blank line: xUnit reported :7 and Fitness reported :6, because a whole-text `(?m)^\s*` match starts on the blank line. Validate can check the patterns with op=rules.

On the worktree, op=check prints no 'MATCHED NO FILES' section, and fit.py reports unmatched=[]. Files covered per entry: screen *.cs 12, screen *.csproj 1, reparse *.cs 12, reparse *.xaml 2, DirectoryReader 7, never-skipped 16, interop (src) 12, interop (tests) 15. Each set is the same as the xUnit Files() set for that [Fact], checked file by file. As a negative control, a typo'd glob (`src/FsAnalyser.Core/*/*.csproj`) came back as unmatched.

The file has a single top-level `rules:` list with two-space-indented mappings, which is what fitness.load (fitness.py:289-318) requires. op=rules lists all 8 entries with their scopes and exemptions. The committed design._append_rules was run on a scratch copy and extended it cleanly: 9 rules after, with the first 8 unchanged.

append.py imported the committed taad3.design and called `_append_rules(tree, [rule], 'SL-999')` on a scratch copy of this file. Results: rules went from 8 to 9, the first 8 were identical in name, files, patterns, except_files, including_comments and because, and the file's original bytes were an unchanged prefix. op=check still passed on 33 files with 0 unmatched. Side observation: the engine appends in Windows text mode, so the appended block is CRLF while the file is LF. It still loads.

`git -C taad_v3 grep -n 'def _append_rules' HEAD -- backend/taad3/design.py` finds it at design.py:1037 in HEAD 0260e7e. `git log -S` shows it arrived in 8f83e23 on 2026-09-12, and `git diff --stat HEAD` on design.py and fitness.py is empty (the only modified files in taad_v3 are the pre-existing backend/tests/conftest.py and backend/tests/test_credentials.py). 0260e7e ('A design accepted after a halt lands everything it settled') is what makes `_record_rules` run on the accepted-after-halt path. That fits SL-020's four declared rules never producing a file, but this is inferred, not traced.
`git check-ignore -v .taad/fitness.yaml .taad/` exits 1 with no match. `git status --short` shows `?? .taad/fitness.yaml`, so it is untracked and not ignored, and `git add -A` will stage it.

deviations: The scope for the csproj half of TheScannerCoreDoesNotKnowAboutTheScreen is written `src/FsAnalyser.Core/**/*.csproj`, not without `**/` as the design said. The design worried that `**/` would need at least one directory in between and so miss FsAnalyser.Core.csproj, which sits directly in its folder (case 9). The engine's `_glob` (fitness.py:201-203) compiles `**/` to `(?:[^/]+/)*`, which also matches zero directories. Measured, the glob covers exactly that one csproj. It also keeps the xUnit scope (SearchOption.AllDirectories) exact, which is the design's main rule. Leaving out `**/` would have narrowed the scope. The negative control showed that a glob which really matches nothing is reported as unmatched.
not_built: No entries in `cases`. The design keeps any converter, parity test or YAML parser out of the .NET project, and no project test feeds a fitness.yaml shape. Pointing at the xUnit twin would claim coverage it does not give. Each shape was measured in a scratch harness instead, as the design prescribed, and the commands and results are listed under `tests`: case 1 (op=rules, plus controls showing a double-quoted `\b` silently stops matching and a double-quoted `\s` makes the loader refuse the file), case 2 (git check-ignore), cases 3-8 and 12 (17 plants and controls), case 9 (coverage counts plus the typo control), case 10 (built tree), case 11 (no-op, see follow-ups).
The mechanism half of C3 (design._append_rules in taad_v3) is engine code outside this worktree. Per Q-009 it is not an SL-022 criterion. I only measured it (O-004, O-005).

C4 is shown with the engine's own fitness module run from the shell, not with the Fitness MCP tool, which the builder is not granted. The design closes C4 only when the '8 rule(s) checked … Every declared rule holds' text appears in this slice's own validate record.
Case 13 (a slice cut before this merges reads NONE) has nothing to build. The design marked it non-material.
Case 14 (a later design appends onto this file) cannot be run through a real design from this repo. It was measured by calling the engine's `_append_rules` on a scratch copy (O-004).
follow_ups: The line number is off for the using-directive rule. `(?m)^\s*using…` matched against whole-file text starts at the first blank line before the offending line: a plant at Scanner.cs:7 after a blank line was reported at :6, while xUnit said :7. Fitness and xUnit still fail on the same rule and file. Fixing it means changing both copies of the rule (for example to `^[ \t]*`), which touches ArchitectureRulesTests and is outside this slice.

Fitness matches `\s`, `[^)]*` and `[^>]*` across line breaks, and xUnit matches one line at a time. That makes Fitness a strict superset: it can fire on a multi-line attribute or project reference that xUnit misses. It is noted in the file header, and nothing in the current tree triggers it.

Engine side (taad_v3): compile must_not_match with MULTILINE, or have the append carry including_comments, so rules a design declares do not silently match less than hand-written ones. Also, the append writes CRLF in text mode on Windows, so the file ends up with mixed line endings. It still loads, and git autocrlf normalises the blob.

Fitness prunes build output only by directory name, so a gitignored directory nested inside a rooted scope (for example src/artifacts/) is read. xUnit reads it too, so the two agree. Honouring .gitignore in the engine would close this.
There is no mechanical guard against the yaml and ArchitectureRulesTests.cs drifting apart. Only the header comment names the twin. The design accepted this risk.
Case 11 is a no-op: no pattern has a `$` anchor. Also, the engine opens files in text mode (fitness.py:422), which already turns CRLF into LF, so even a `$` anchor would work without `\r?`.
Remember that `python -m taad3.fitness --op check` exits 0 even when it prints VIOLATED. Any gate built on it must read the report text.

tests.note: Expected, and outside the design's case-10 shape. Fitness read src/artifacts/Planted.cs and Planted.xaml (35 files) and reported 7 violations. xUnit failed the same two Facts on the same files, so the two agree. The probe directory was removed afterwards and the built tree re-checked clean.

Six negative controls, each run on a fresh copy. Typo glob: reported as unmatched. except_files removed: fails at Kernel32.cs:23,67,72, EntryClassifier.cs:26 and TestNative.cs:12, so the exemptions are needed and each is exact to one file. Double-quoted `\b`: a planted 0x400 silently passes. Double-quoted `\s`: the loader refuses with 'unknown escape character s'. No (?m): a planted using on line 6 silently passes. No including_comments: a comment DllImport passes, reported under IN COMMENTS.

Imported the committed taad3.design._append_rules. 8 rules became 9, the hand-written entries and bytes were unchanged, and op=check still passes on 33 files with 0 unmatched. The appended block is CRLF.
86 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. This is the project's full suite, including the unchanged ArchitectureRulesTests twin.
